newsitem.title: USA: Group wins right to appeal IBM court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Group wins right to appeal IBM court ruling.

text.p: The Independent Service Network International (ISNI) said Tuesday it won the right to appeal a federal court decision to terminate the consent decree agreed to by International Business Machines Corp and the U.S. government in 1956.
A federal district court judge in Manhattan granted ISNI, a trade association of independent maintainers of high technology equipment, the right to appeal his ruling in a June 26 order.

The consent decree, a result of an antitrust action against the company in 1952, required IBM to segregate its computer services operations into a separate unit paying full retail price for equipment and software it bought from IBM to resell to customers.
The decree also required the company to sell parts to independent service organizations, ISNI said.
On May 1, the court upheld an agreement to terminate the decree in stages over a five-year period.
In an order dated June 26, the court granted ISNI's motion to file an appeal because the group's contentions deserve the attention of the court, ISNI said.
The only entity arguing against termination, ISNI said it had to ask the court's permission to appeal the matter because it was not a party to the lawsuit.
ISNI, based in Atlanta, said it represents 200 computer and medical technology maintainers.
